newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has pledged to use his leadership to revive the economy and inspire foreign investors' confidence. His pledge came as the Foreign Chambers of Commerce issued a thinly-veiled warning to him that overseas investors are fed up with governmental mismanagement of Thailand's economy and vested-interest politics. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- U.S. President Bill Clinton has commended Thailand for showing that democracy and economic growth can go together, and promised to help restore trading privileges. He said the U.S. would continue to maintain its strong military presence in Asia and the Pacific to protect the common security, and would reinforce its relations with the five core regional alliances - Australia, Japan, the Philippines, South Korea and Thailand. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The new Cabinet line-up is nearing completion with Prachuab Chaisarn expected to be foreign minister while the Interior Ministry looks likely to have an unprecedented five deputy ministers. Amnuay Viravan is set to become finance minister and deputy prime minister but his hope of leading an economic "Dream Team" has been watered down to a trio whose future cooperation with the Chart Pattana Party is questionable. (THE NATION)

- Chalongphob Sussangkarn, president of the Thailand Development Research Institute, has suggested that the new government ought to revise the eighth national economic plan by reducing annual economic growth to between 6-7 percent instead of 8 percent targeted earlier. The reduction, he said, would help reduce business damages in both the private and public sectors. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)

- International Business Machines Corp, the world's largest computer company, plans to invest in a hard-disk drive production facility on the Eastern Seaboard - propelling Thailand towards its goal of becoming a regional hub for the computer and electronics industry. (THE NATION)
